learn.hook: Why can a bamboo shoot grow taller every day, and why is a coconut husk so tough that you need a sickle to open it? Different plant tissues are the answer!
points: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to do a particular job.

Meristematic tissue has actively dividing cells with dense cytoplasm and thin walls. Apical meristem at root and shoot tips increases length; lateral meristem (cambium) increases girth; intercalary meristem at the base of leaves or internodes (as in grasses) adds length there.

Simple permanent tissues: parenchyma (thin-walled, stores food; chlorenchyma has chlorophyll; aerenchyma has big air spaces that help water plants float), collenchyma (walls thickened at the corners, gives flexibility to leaf stalks) and sclerenchyma (dead cells with thick lignin walls, gives hardness, as in coconut husk).

Complex permanent tissues are made of more than one type of cell: xylem (tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, xylem fibres) carries water and minerals; phloem (sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, phloem fibres) carries food.
Protective tissues: the epidermis covers the plant, often with a waxy cuticle, and older stems are covered by cork, whose dead cells contain suberin.

example.q: Think it through: A lotus plant floats easily on a pond. Which tissue helps, and how?
steps: The stems and leaf stalks of water plants have parenchyma with large air cavities.
This special parenchyma is called aerenchyma.
The trapped air makes the parts light.
So the plant gets buoyancy and floats.
example.answer: Aerenchyma, a parenchyma with large air spaces, gives buoyancy.

learn.reallife: Coir mats and ropes made in Kerala come from the tough sclerenchyma fibres of coconut husk, and jute bags are made from plant fibres too.

games.title: Match the tissue to the clue
pairs: Growth in length at root and shoot tips
Growth in girth of the stem

games.title: Simple or complex?
items: Tissue made of sieve tubes and companion cells
Tissue made of tracheids and vessels

quiz.q: Which tissue makes a root or a shoot grow longer at its tip?
quiz.explain: Apical meristem is present at the growing tips of roots and stems and increases their length.
steps: Meristems are regions of actively dividing cells.
Apical meristem at root and shoot tips increases length.
Lateral meristem adds girth; cork and sclerenchyma do not divide.
Answer: Apical meristem
quiz.mistake: Mixes up apical meristem (length) with lateral meristem (girth)

quiz.q: The trunk of a neem tree becomes thicker every year. Which tissue causes this?
quiz.explain: Lateral meristem, also called cambium, divides to increase the girth of stems and roots.
steps: The trunk gets thicker: an increase in girth.
Lateral meristem (cambium) increases girth.
Apical meristem only adds length.
Answer: Lateral meristem (cambium)
quiz.mistake: Thinks the growing tip also makes the stem thicker

quiz.q: The husk of a coconut is made of which tissue?
quiz.explain: Coconut husk has sclerenchyma fibres: dead cells with thick, lignified walls that make it hard.
steps: Coconut husk is hard and fibrous.
Sclerenchyma: dead cells with thick lignin walls, giving hardness.
Answer: Sclerenchyma
quiz.mistake: Confuses tough sclerenchyma with soft storage parenchyma

quiz.q: Which tissue helps aquatic plants like water hyacinth float?
quiz.explain: Aerenchyma is parenchyma with large air cavities that give buoyancy.
steps: Floating needs air inside the plant body.
Aerenchyma is parenchyma with big air spaces that give buoyancy.
Answer: Aerenchyma
quiz.mistake: Does not know that parenchyma can have air spaces

quiz.q: Which tissue lets the leaf stalk bend in the wind without breaking?
quiz.explain: Collenchyma cells are living, with walls thickened only at the corners, giving support with flexibility.
steps: The leaf stalk must bend without breaking: flexible support.
Collenchyma has walls thickened only at the corners and gives flexibility.
Sclerenchyma is rigid, not flexible.
Answer: Collenchyma
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hardest tissue, sclerenchyma, gives flexibility

quiz.q: Which tissue carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves?
quiz.explain: Xylem, made of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres, carries water and dissolved minerals upwards.
steps: Complex tissues: xylem carries water and minerals; phloem carries food.
Roots to leaves = water and minerals.
Answer: Xylem
quiz.mistake: Mixes up xylem (water) with phloem (food)

quiz.q: Which tissue carries food made in the leaves to other parts of the plant?
quiz.explain: Phloem, made of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres, carries food.
steps: Food made in leaves must move to other parts.
Phloem carries food; xylem carries water.
Answer: Phloem
quiz.mistake: Thinks xylem carries both water and food

quiz.q: Desert plants have a thick waxy cuticle on their epidermis. What is its main use?
options: To absorb more water from the air
To help the plant grow taller
quiz.explain: The waxy cuticle is water-resistant, so it cuts down water loss in hot, dry places.
steps: The epidermis is often covered by a waxy cuticle.
Wax is water-resistant, so it cuts water loss in hot, dry places.
Answer: To reduce loss of water
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cuticle helps take in water rather than keep it in

teach.ask: Gappu is resting on a mango branch: "How does this tree grow taller, get thicker AND move water all the way up to the leaves?"
teach.praise: Chirp! Meristems divide to make the tree longer and thicker, permanent tissues support and store, xylem lifts water and phloem carries food. Clever tree!
teach.nudge: And which tissue carries the water up, and which one carries the food?

revise.summary: A tissue is a group of similar cells doing one job. Plants have dividing meristems and permanent tissues: simple (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma), complex (xylem, phloem) and protective (epidermis, cork).
focus: Apical, lateral and intercalary meristems and where they act
Parenchyma types, collenchyma and sclerenchyma with examples
Xylem vs phloem: parts and what they carry
Epidermis with cuticle, and cork with suberin
remember: Apical → length; lateral (cambium) → girth; intercalary → base of leaves/internodes
Aerenchyma = air spaces, floating; collenchyma = flexibility; sclerenchyma = lignin, hardness
Xylem = water and minerals; phloem = food
Cork cells are dead and contain suberin
traps: Don't say apical meristem increases girth
Sclerenchyma cells are dead; collenchyma cells are living

learn.hook: When you kick a football, three of the four main kinds of animal tissue work together in your leg in a split second: muscle, nerve and connective tissue such as bone and blood!
points: Epithelial tissue covers and lines the body. Squamous epithelium lines the mouth and blood vessels; skin has many layers (stratified squamous); cuboidal epithelium lines kidney tubules; columnar epithelium lines the intestine; ciliated columnar epithelium lines the windpipe.

Connective tissue joins and supports. Blood has a fluid matrix (plasma); bone is hard with calcium and phosphorus compounds; cartilage supports the nose and ear; tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone; areolar tissue fills spaces; adipose tissue stores fat.

Muscular tissue contracts to cause movement. Striated (skeletal) muscle is voluntary; smooth (unstriated) muscle is involuntary, as in the intestine and iris; cardiac muscle of the heart is involuntary and contracts rhythmically all through life.
Nervous tissue is made of neurons. A neuron has a cell body with a nucleus, short branched dendrites and a long axon. Neurons carry messages called nerve impulses.

example.q: Think it through: Sana twists her ankle while playing kho-kho and the doctor says a ligament is stretched. What does a ligament do?
steps: Bones at a joint must be held together but still be able to move.
Ligaments are connective tissue that join one bone to another.
They are strong and elastic.
A sudden twist can over-stretch them, causing pain and swelling.
example.answer: A ligament joins bone to bone at a joint; Sana's ankle ligament was over-stretched.

learn.reallife: Physiotherapists who help cricketers recover from injuries need to know exactly which muscles, tendons and ligaments are affected.

games.title: Match the tissue to where it is found
Animal tissues: true or false?
items: Blood has cells floating in a fluid matrix called plasma, so it is a connective tissue.
Cardiac muscle is a voluntary muscle
You cannot control your heartbeat by choice; cardiac muscle is involuntary.
Tendons are strong connective tissue that pull on bones when muscles contract.
The axon carries the nerve impulse away from the cell body
Dendrites bring messages in; the axon carries them away to the next cell.
Smooth muscle is found in the muscles of the arm that lift a school bag
Lifting a bag uses striated (skeletal) muscle, which is voluntary.

quiz.q: Which tissue joins a muscle to a bone?
quiz.explain: Tendons are strong fibrous connective tissue joining muscles to bones.
steps: Connective tissue: tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.
Answer: Tendon
quiz.mistake: Mixes up tendon (muscle to bone) with ligament (bone to bone)

quiz.q: Which tissue joins one bone to another bone?
quiz.explain: Ligaments are elastic connective tissue that hold bones together at joints.
steps: Ligaments join bone to bone at joints.
Tendons join muscle to bone.
Answer: Ligament
quiz.mistake: Thinks tendons hold bones together

quiz.q: The inner lining of the mouth is made of which tissue?
quiz.explain: Thin, flat squamous epithelial cells line the mouth and blood vessels.
steps: Epithelium covers and lines the body.
Squamous epithelium lines the mouth and blood vessels.
Answer: Squamous epithelium
quiz.mistake: Does not know that linings of body cavities are epithelial tissue

quiz.q: Why is blood called a connective tissue?
options: It has cells in a fluid matrix and connects body parts by transport
It is a solid tissue like bone
quiz.explain: Blood has RBCs, WBCs and platelets in liquid plasma, and it carries materials between all parts of the body.
steps: Blood has cells (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) in a fluid matrix, plasma.
It carries materials between all body parts, so it connects them.
Answer: It has cells in a fluid matrix and connects body parts by transport
quiz.mistake: Thinks a tissue must be solid

quiz.q: Which tissue stores fat below the skin and helps insulate the body?
quiz.explain: Adipose tissue cells are filled with fat globules, which store energy and reduce heat loss.
steps: Adipose tissue stores fat.
Fat below the skin stores energy and reduces heat loss.
Answer: Adipose tissue
quiz.mistake: Confuses fat-storing tissue with supporting tissues

quiz.q: Which muscle is involuntary, has branched cells and contracts rhythmically throughout life?
quiz.explain: Cardiac (heart) muscle cells are branched and cylindrical and keep contracting rhythmically all through life.
steps: Striated muscle is voluntary; smooth muscle is involuntary but not rhythmic all life.
Cardiac muscle is involuntary and contracts rhythmically all through life.
Answer: Cardiac muscle
quiz.mistake: Knows the heart is involuntary but labels it smooth muscle

quiz.q: Which part of a neuron carries a nerve impulse away from the cell body?
quiz.explain: The axon is the long fibre that carries impulses away from the cell body. Dendrites receive impulses.
steps: A neuron has a cell body, dendrites and a long axon.
Dendrites receive impulses; the axon carries them away from the cell body.
Answer: Axon
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the axon and the dendrites

quiz.q: The bendable part of your outer ear is supported by
quiz.explain: Cartilage is a firm but flexible connective tissue that supports the ear and the tip of the nose.
steps: Cartilage supports the nose and ear.
It is firm but flexible, so the outer ear bends.
Answer: cartilage
quiz.mistake: Thinks every supporting tissue must be bone

teach.ask: Gappu wiggles his toes: "How many kinds of tissue does an animal have, and what does each one do?"
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Epithelial tissue covers, connective tissue joins and supports, muscle moves and nerves carry messages. Four teams in one body!
teach.nudge: You told me about some tissues, but which tissue carries messages from my brain to my wings?

revise.summary: Animal tissues are epithelial (cover and line), connective (join and support), muscular (contract) and nervous (carry impulses). Each type has sub-types suited to particular places and jobs.
focus: Types of epithelium and where each is found
Connective tissues: blood, bone, cartilage, tendon, ligament, areolar, adipose
remember: Tendon = muscle to bone; ligament = bone to bone
Cardiac muscle: involuntary, branched, rhythmic all life
Axon carries impulses away from the cell body; dendrites receive
traps: Smooth muscle is involuntary, striated muscle is voluntary
Blood is a connective tissue, not epithelial

topics.title: Tissues at work: structure and function

learn.hook: On a hot afternoon a peepal tree can lose many buckets of water through its leaves, and still keep lifting more from the soil. How do its tissues manage this?
points: Every tissue is built to suit its job: thick lignin walls for strength, air spaces for floating, long axons for carrying messages over long distances.
Xylem carries water and minerals only upwards from roots; phloem carries food in both directions, from leaves to roots, fruits and growing parts.
Stomata are tiny pores in the leaf epidermis, each opened and closed by two guard cells. They allow exchange of gases and loss of water vapour (transpiration).
Ciliated epithelium in the windpipe sweeps mucus and trapped dust upwards. Smooth muscle in the intestine pushes food along without our control.
Blood transports materials: red blood cells carry oxygen, white blood cells fight infection and platelets help blood to clot.

example.q: Think it through: A potted plant's leaves droop on a hot day, but recover in the evening after watering. Explain using tissues.
steps: Leaves lose water vapour through stomata during transpiration, more on hot days.
If water is lost faster than xylem can bring it up, the cells lose water and the leaves droop.
After watering, roots absorb water and xylem carries it to the leaves.
The cells fill with water again and become firm, so the leaves stand up.
example.answer: Water lost through stomata was replaced when xylem brought fresh water to the leaves.

learn.reallife: Gardeners water plants in the early morning or evening, when less water is lost through stomata.

games.title: The journey of water in a plant
games.prompt: Trace water from the soil to the air
items: Root hairs absorb water from the soil
Water enters the xylem of the root
Xylem of the stem carries it upwards
Water reaches the veins of the leaf

quiz.q: Which pair of cells opens and closes a stoma?
quiz.explain: Each stoma is bordered by two kidney-shaped guard cells that change shape to open or close the pore.
steps: Each stoma is a tiny pore in the leaf epidermis.
It is opened and closed by two guard cells.
Answer: Guard cells
quiz.mistake: Confuses guard cells with cells of the phloem

quiz.q: Which two jobs do stomata perform?
quiz.explain: Carbon dioxide and oxygen pass through stomata, and water vapour escapes through them during transpiration.
steps: Stomata allow gases (CO₂, O₂) in and out.
Water vapour also escapes through them: transpiration.
Answer: Exchange of gases and transpiration
quiz.mistake: Thinks stomata transport materials like xylem and phloem

quiz.q: Sugar made in mango leaves reaches the ripening fruit and the roots. Which tissue carries it, and in which direction?
quiz.explain: Phloem carries food from the leaves to wherever it is needed, up or down. Xylem carries water only upwards.
steps: Sugar is food, so it moves in phloem.
Fruit and roots lie in different directions from the leaves.
Phloem carries food both ways; xylem carries water only upwards.
Answer: Phloem, in both directions
quiz.mistake: Thinks food moves only downwards, or that xylem carries food

quiz.q: Food keeps moving through your intestine even when you are asleep. Which tissue does this?
quiz.explain: Smooth muscle in the wall of the alimentary canal contracts on its own, without conscious control.
steps: Movement while asleep happens without our control.
Smooth muscle in the intestine is involuntary and pushes food along.
Striated muscle is voluntary.
Answer: Smooth muscle
quiz.mistake: Thinks all muscle movement needs us to decide it

quiz.q: What is the job of the ciliated epithelium lining the windpipe?
options: To sweep mucus and trapped dust out of the airway
quiz.explain: The cilia beat together and move dust-trapping mucus up and away from the lungs.
steps: Ciliated epithelium lines the windpipe.
Its cilia sweep mucus and trapped dust upwards, away from the lungs.
Answer: To sweep mucus and trapped dust out of the airway
quiz.mistake: Does not link cilia with movement of mucus

quiz.q: Which part of blood helps a small cut stop bleeding by forming a clot?
quiz.explain: Platelets help blood to clot and seal the wound.
steps: Blood parts: RBCs carry oxygen, WBCs fight infection, platelets help clotting.
A clot stops bleeding.
Answer: Platelets
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the jobs of the different blood components

quiz.q: Why are bones hard and strong?
options: They are made of muscle fibres
They are hollow and full of air
Their matrix contains calcium and phosphorus compounds
quiz.explain: Bone cells sit in a hard matrix made of calcium and phosphorus compounds, giving the body a strong frame.
steps: Bone is a connective tissue with a hard matrix.
The matrix contains calcium and phosphorus compounds.
Answer: Their matrix contains calcium and phosphorus compounds
quiz.mistake: Does not know what gives bone its hardness

quiz.q: Why are sclerenchyma cells good at making plant parts hard?
options: They have thin walls and big vacuoles
They have thick walls hardened with lignin
quiz.explain: Lignin is a cementing substance that thickens and hardens the walls of sclerenchyma cells.
steps: Sclerenchyma gives hardness.
Its walls are thick and hardened with lignin.
Answer: They have thick walls hardened with lignin
quiz.mistake: Thinks living, dividing cells make tissues hard

teach.ask: Gappu drinks from a puddle: "How does water climb all the way up a tree, and where does it go after that?"
teach.praise: Chirp! Roots absorb water, xylem carries it up to the leaves and it escapes as vapour through the stomata. Trees are amazing water pumps!
teach.nudge: Once the water reaches the leaves, how does it get out into the air?

revise.summary: Each tissue's structure suits its job. Xylem carries water up, phloem carries food both ways, guard cells control stomata, cilia sweep the windpipe, smooth muscle moves food and blood transports materials.
focus: Linking structure to function in plant and animal tissues
Direction of transport in xylem and phloem
Jobs of RBCs, WBCs and platelets
remember: Xylem: upwards only; phloem: both directions
Stomata: gas exchange and transpiration; opened/closed by guard cells
RBCs carry oxygen; WBCs fight infection; platelets clot blood
Bone matrix: calcium and phosphorus compounds
traps: Phloem is not one-way like xylem
Food moves in the intestine by smooth, not striated, muscle
Stomata are opened by guard cells, not companion cells
